findings.title: Calendar updates use the guest-adder's credentials instead of the organizer's
findings.body: The mutation explicitly authorizes any existing attendee to add guests, but it builds EventManager with credentials from ctx.user. For an attendee or a team admin who is not the booking organizer, those credentials normally cannot edit the organizer's calendar event, so updateCalendarAttendees will fail or leave the organizer's event unchanged. The booking attendee rows have already been written at this point, producing an inconsistent booking and calendar state.

findings.title: Guest records are committed before calendar synchronization can fail
findings.body: The attendee rows are persisted before updateCalendarAttendees is called. If the calendar provider rejects the update or a network error occurs, the mutation returns an error even though the guests remain in the database. Retrying the same request then fails because the guests are no longer considered new, leaving no way for the caller to retry calendar synchronization and no notification sent to the added guests.

findings.title: Team admin-or-owner authorization is implemented as admin-and-owner
findings.body: The permission check uses && between isTeamAdmin and isTeamOwner, despite the variable and intended policy being admin-or-owner. A normal team ADMIN membership does not satisfy the owner check, and an OWNER may not satisfy an admin-only check, so team users who should be allowed to manage the booking are rejected unless they also happen to be the organizer or an attendee.

findings.title: The server accepts duplicate guest addresses in one request
findings.body: Uniqueness is only checked by the dialog's client-side schema; this public tRPC input schema accepts repeated emails. The handler filters only against attendees that existed before the request, so repeated values are all passed to createMany and the calendar/email paths. Direct API callers can therefore create duplicate attendee rows and duplicate invitations, or cause the entire write to fail if a database uniqueness constraint is added later.

findings.title: Guest additions have no server-side batch limit
findings.body: The guests array is unbounded, while any authenticated attendee is authorized to invoke this endpoint. A caller can submit thousands of arbitrary addresses, causing an unbounded createMany, calendar update, translation work, and Promise.all email fan-out from the organizer's account. This enables bulk invitation spam and can exhaust request worker resources; the endpoint needs an enforced maximum or controlled batching/rate limit.

findings.title: Cancelled and rejected bookings can still receive new guests
findings.body: After finding and authorizing the booking, the handler never checks its status or whether the event has already ended. An authenticated attendee can call the tRPC endpoint for a CANCELLED or REJECTED booking, create attendee records, update the calendar, and send emails whose generated ICS status is CONFIRMED. This can effectively re-invite people to an event that should no longer accept attendees.

findings.title: Add-guest notifications ignore disableStandardEmails preferences
findings.body: Unlike the scheduled, rescheduled, cancelled, and location-change email helpers, sendAddGuestsEmails neither accepts event-type metadata nor checks eventTypeDisableHostEmail/eventTypeDisableAttendeeEmail. Consequently, an event type configured to disable all standard host or attendee emails will still send organizer and attendee add-guest messages, violating the event type's notification setting.

findings.title: Email classification uses requested guests rather than guests actually added
findings.body: uniqueGuests filters out addresses that were already attendees, but sendAddGuestsEmails receives the original guests array. For example, submitting an existing attendee plus one new address succeeds, yet the existing attendee is treated as a new guest and receives an AttendeeScheduledEmail rather than the guest-added update. Pass uniqueGuests so notification type and recipients reflect the database change.

findings.title: Team members are never included in add-guest notifications
findings.body: The CalendarEvent constructed here never sets team, and the Prisma eventType include does not load its team relation or members. sendAddGuestsEmails only sends organizer updates to additional team members through calendarEvent.team.members, so that branch is always skipped for this handler. Team members other than the assigned booking user will not be notified when guests are added.

findings.title: Blacklisted guest emails can be bypassed with casing changes
findings.body: BLACKLISTED_GUEST_EMAILS is normalized to lowercase, but each submitted guest address is compared without lowercasing. A blacklist entry such as blocked@example.com does not match BLOCKED@example.com, allowing a caller to invite an address the deployment has explicitly blocked. Normalize submitted addresses before both blacklist and existing-attendee comparisons.
